lesson.text: Quick memory: what is a collage? (A picture made by sticking on materials.) Today: art you can walk round.
A sculpture is 3D art: it has height, width and depth, so you can walk all the way round it. A drawing on paper is flat (2D).
Sculptors carve (cut material away, like stone or wood), model (shape clay with their hands) or construct (join pieces together).
A good sculpture looks interesting from every side: the front, the back, the left, the right and even from above. Walk round it and check each view.
Sculptures need balance: a wide, heavy base keeps them standing. Tall, thin parts need support.
Building with blocks in this game is constructing! Every build is a sculpture you can walk round, fly over and look at from below.
Some of the oldest art in the world is sculpture: people carved small animals and figures from stone and mammoth ivory more than 30,000 years ago.
Try it in the world: build a sculpture of an animal from blocks. Walk all the way round it and fly above it. Fix any side that looks flat or empty.

exercises.explain: A sculpture is 3D art, with height, width and depth: you can walk round it.

exercises.prompt: A drawing on paper is 2D, and a sculpture is 3D.
exercises.hint: Flat, or can you walk round it?
exercises.explain: True: a drawing is flat (2D); a sculpture has depth too (3D).
2D: painting, drawing, photo. 3D: clay pot, statue, block tower.

exercises.prompt: From how many sides should you check a sculpture?
exercises.hint: People can walk all the way round it.
exercises.explain: Check it from every side, and from above too.

exercises.prompt: Match each way of making a sculpture to what you do.
exercises.hint: Carve like a woodcutter, model like a potter, construct like a builder.
exercises.explain: Carving cuts material away, modelling shapes clay, constructing joins pieces together.

choices: cutting a shape out of a block of wood
exercises.explain: Cutting a shape out of wood is carving: material is taken away.

exercises.prompt: Building a statue from blocks in this game is…
exercises.explain: Constructing: you join blocks together to build it.

exercises.prompt: A tall, thin sculpture with a tiny base can fall over easily.
exercises.hint: Think of balancing a pencil on its end.
exercises.explain: True: a wide, heavy base keeps a sculpture standing.

exercises.prompt: Zara's block dragon looks great from the front, but its back is flat and empty. What should she do?
exercises.hint: A sculpture is seen from every side.
choices: walk round and add detail to the back
only show it from the front
exercises.explain: Walk round and add detail to the back, so it looks good from every side.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps for building a block sculpture in a sensible order.
exercises.hint: Plan first; the base holds everything up.
exercises.explain: Plan the big shapes, build a strong base, build the body, then walk round adding details.

exercises.prompt: Which is the best base for a tall tower sculpture?
exercises.hint: What keeps something from tipping over?
exercises.explain: A wide, heavy base keeps a tall sculpture steady: its weight is low down and spread out, so a push or the wind cannot tip it over.

exercises.prompt: About how long ago did people carve small animal figures from mammoth ivory?
exercises.hint: Mammoths lived in the Ice Age.
exercises.explain: More than 30,000 years ago, when mammoths still lived.

exercises.prompt: Looking at a sculpture from above can show you things you can't see from the side.
exercises.hint: Fly over one of your builds. What do you notice?
exercises.explain: True: the top view shows the shape in a new way.

exercises.prompt: Which word means art that has height, width and depth?
exercises.explain: 3D: three dimensions. Height is how tall, width how wide and depth how far back it goes. A drawing has only height and width: 2D.

exercises.hint: Taking material away, or joining pieces together?
exercises.explain: Carving: chipping stone, cutting a spoon from wood. Constructing: the box robot, the block castle.

exercises.prompt: Bram builds a solid block tower 3 blocks wide, 3 blocks deep and 4 blocks high. How many blocks does he use?
exercises.hint: Count the blocks in one layer first. Then count the layers.
exercises.explain: One layer is 3 wide and 3 deep: 3 × 3 = 9 blocks. There are 4 layers: 9 × 4 = 36 blocks. Width, depth and height: that is 3D!
